{{nihongo|'''Hisashi Matsuda'''|松田 久||2 March 1924 - 13 November 2011}}<ref name="urlHisashi Matsuda (1924–2011)">{{cite journal |title=Hisashi Matsuda (1924–2011) |year=2012 |pmc=4570945 |last1=Toyoda |first1=M. |journal=Mass Spectrometry |volume=1 |issue=2 |article-number=K0003 |doi=10.5702/massspectrometry.K0003 }}</ref> was a [[Japan|Japanese]] physicist known for his work in [[ion optics]] and [[mass spectrometry]], specifically known for his contributions to instrument design.<ref name="encyclopedia">{{cite book |editor1-last=Gross |editor1-first=Michael L. |editor2-last=Caprioli |editor2-first=Richard M. |title=The Encyclopedia of Mass Spectrometry |date=2015 |isbn=978-0-08-100379-4 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/book/9780081003794/the-encyclopedia-of-mass-spectrometry }}{{pn|date=April 2021}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Matsuda was born in [[Osaka]] and studied physics and mathematics at [[Osaka University]], receiving a PhD in 1957 from Osaka University for his thesis on mass spectrometry under [[Koreichi Ogata]].<ref name="encyclopedia"/> He started as assistant professor in 1955 and become associate professor in 1959 and full professor 1963 at Osaka University.<ref name="encyclopedia"/> His career was devoted to mass spectrometry, developing novel ion optics and improving [[Resolution (mass spectrometry)|resolving power]].<ref name="encyclopedia"/> In 1956 he constructed the Ogata–Matsuda type instrument with a mass resolution of 900,000 which was the highest resolution worldwide.<ref name="urlHisashi Matsuda (1924–2011)"/> He constructed mass spectrometers suited for analysis of large biomolecules and was one of the first to realize the implications of mass spectrometry on the analysis of peptides and proteins.<ref name="encyclopedia"/> He retired in 1987.

He was awarded several prizes for his work, including the Nishina Memorial Prize in 1969 and the Toray Science and Technology Prize in 1982.<ref name="urlHisashi Matsuda (1924–2011)"/> He received the Thomson medal from the International Mass Spectrometry Society in 1991 and the Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with a Neck Ribbon in spring 2002.<ref name="urlHisashi Matsuda (1924–2011)"/>
